profile.campus: Suwanee, Gwinnett County, Georgia (QTS Suwanee campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, Suwanee DC2 sits at 120 Satellite Blvd NW, Suwanee, GA 30024, part of a 53-acre campus with 50+ MW critical capacity currently, with 100+ MW planned.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists an operations support center in Suwanee, Georgia, making this Atlanta-metro cluster (Atlanta proper, Suwanee/Gwinnett County, and Fayetteville/Fayette County) an operationally significant hub for the company beyond its Northern Virginia headquarters.

Georgia Power, the state's dominant investor-owned electric utility, has flagged data center load growth in its own integrated resource plan filings with state regulators as a major driver of future generation and transmission investment, a pattern also seen among Northern Virginia's Dominion Energy and Texas's ERCOT grid operator elsewhere in this registry. Metro Atlanta's data center growth has also drawn legislative attention over sales-tax exemptions for data center equipment, a policy debate covered in Georgia trade and political press as the industry has expanded across Fulton, Gwinnett, Fayette, and neighboring counties.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne, both also present in the metro Atlanta market. Under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its Georgia footprint, including the still-under-development Fayetteville mega-campus tracked elsewhere in this registry, rather than slowing investment after going private.

reading.body:
QTS Suwanee DC2 sits on a 53-acre campus in Gwinnett County with 50+ MW of critical capacity operating today and 100+ MW planned. The facility is part of QTS's Atlanta-metro cluster, one of the company's operationally significant hubs since its 2003 founding. At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, the current 50 MW critical load translates to roughly 1,250 racks, with potential to reach 2,500 racks at full planned capacity.

Georgia Power, the state's dominant utility, has flagged data center load growth as a major driver of future generation and transmission investment in its regulatory filings. The Suwanee campus contributes to a state total of 66.3 MW of published capacity across four facilities, ranking fifth in the state by published megawattage. The company operates as a hyperscale-neutral wholesale colocation landlord rather than an end-user cloud operator, leasing built capacity to enterprise and cloud tenants.

QTS was taken private by Blackstone in a $10 billion acquisition completed in 2021 and continues to expand its Georgia footprint despite the going-private transition. The state context shows 33 facilities mapped in Georgia but only 4 with published specifications, indicating most data center capacity in the state remains undisclosed. This campus's published commitment to double capacity reflects confidence in metro Atlanta's continued appeal as a data center market.
